_about: Big moment scenes. Each plays once (big moments, and smaller ones like Cheddar inviting you on beach trips), at closing after the last customer leaves, when its regular meets 'conditions' (the same conditions dialogue lines use). Steps run in order: 'narrate' (stage directions, no speaker), 'say' (the regular, optionally with 'choices': each { text, reply }), 'cook' (the co-cooking minigame at the stove: it can't fail). 'staging': dim (light multiplier), music (the scene's song; without one, music_db is how far the usual music drops), rain, flicker. 'done' sets memory fields and unlocks rewards (flags in GameState.unlocks for now).

reward_names.best_chef_sign: "World's Best Chef (don't tell anyone I said that)" sign
reward_names.cheddar_car: Beach trips in Cheddar's car (after hours, out front)
reward_names.mabel_house: Visits to Mabel's house (after hours, knock)
reward_names.stitches_house: Visits to Stitches' house (after hours, knock)
reward_names.cheddar_house: Visits to Cheddar's house (after hours, knock)

steps.narrate: (Stitches comes in holding a bundle wrapped in brown paper. For the first time in weeks, he is fidgeting with his ear patch.)

steps.say: Hi, [name]. Sorry. I know you're closing. I'm nervous. ...I'm doing the ear thing again. I haven't done that in a long time.
I made you something. It took me a while. Every night for a few weeks.

steps.narrate: (He unwraps it: a patchwork apron in mismatched fabrics.)

steps.say: Every patch is from something. The blue one is from my old blanket. This one with the stars, you remember that one? And this one is from the scarf I wore the first day I came here. I was so scared that day. I almost didn't come in.

choices.reply: You really think so? ...You always say things like you mean them.

choices.text: You made all of this for me?
choices.reply: Of course for you. Who else?

choices.text: I'm going to wear it every day.
choices.reply: Every day? Okay. Now I have to make sure it's sturdy.

steps.say: Before I found this place, I ate alone every day. I thought that's just what I was. Someone people put up with.
And then you were nice to me. Not once. Every time. Even when I was weird. Even when I said sorry too much.
You never laughed at my patches. You asked about them. Nobody had ever done that.
I sat at a middle table last week. I said hi to a stranger at the park. I like myself now. Most days. ...That's because of you.
You changed my life, [name]. I just wanted you to know.

choices.text: You did all of that. I just made the food.
choices.reply: Maybe. But you made it like I mattered.

choices.text: Okay, now YOU'RE going to make ME cry.
choices.reply: (He laughs through tears.) Good. Then we're even.

choices.text: You're my favorite customer. You always were.
choices.reply: (A long pause. He hugs you.)

steps.say: Okay. I'm going to go before I cry in your restaurant. ...Too late. Goodnight, [name].

steps.narrate: (He wipes his eyes with his patched arm, waves at the door, waves again, and leaves.)
(Cheddar bursts in wearing a chef's hat that's way too big for him. It covers his eyes.)

steps.say: Nobody panic! It's me! I'm the chef tonight. You're the customer. Sit. SIT. That's an order, customer.

steps.narrate: (You sit at a table, for the first time ever. Cheddar disappears into the kitchen. Clanging. A small crash.)

steps.say: I'm fine!

steps.narrate: (He comes out with a plate of [player_favorite]. It's lopsided, a little burnt on one side, and decorated with a tiny paper flag that says "for [name].")

steps.say: Okay. So. It's not as good as yours. It's not even as good as your bad days. But I made it.

choices.reply: Obviously. You remember mine. That's how this works.
It's CHARACTER. I learned that from you.
(He watches you, tail completely still.) ...Well?? Say something!

steps.narrate: (He sits across from you and takes his hat off. For a second, he doesn't say anything.)

steps.say: I'm gonna say something and I'm not gonna make a joke after it. Which is gonna be really hard for me. So just let me get through it.
My whole life, people liked me when I was funny. That's it. That was the deal. Be funny, or be invisible.
And then I come here and you laugh at my jokes, sure. But you also ask how I'm actually doing. And you notice when I'm quiet. And you never, ever give me cheese.
You're the first person who made me feel like I don't have to perform to be worth having around. ...So, thank you. That's it. That's the whole thing.

steps.narrate: (He holds very still, clearly fighting the urge to add a joke.)

choices.text: You were always worth having around. Jokes or no jokes.
choices.reply: (His eyes get shiny.) ...Okay. Okay. I need a minute.

choices.text: You can make a joke now. You've earned it.
choices.reply: OH THANK GOODNESS. Okay: what do you call a mouse who cooks? ...Me. Tonight. Ha! I'm crying a little.

choices.text: I'm really glad you came into my restaurant.
choices.reply: ...Me too, partner. Me too.

steps.say: Okay. Wash the plate yourself, customer. I'm a chef, not a dishwasher. ...Goodnight, [name].

steps.narrate: (Mabel comes in with a small tin box under her arm and a wet umbrella.)

steps.say: Don't close up yet, dear. I've come to cook.
I haven't cooked for anyone in eleven years. I'd like to again. Tonight. With you.

steps.narrate: (She opens the tin. Inside is a single recipe card, stained and soft with age, and a small brass bell.)

steps.say: Walter's soup. The one from the storm. He never wrote anything down except this.

steps.rescue: (She quietly turns the burner down for you.)

steps.say: I promised you the end of the story. Here it is.

At dawn the storm passed. Everyone went home. And that young cook brought me the very last bowl. He'd salted it. He said, 'You're the only one who told me the truth last night. Would you stay for breakfast?'
I stayed fifty years.

choices.text: That's the most beautiful story I've ever heard.
choices.reply: It is, isn't it. I've been saving it for the right person.

choices.text: Did the soup need salt tonight?
choices.reply: (She tastes it.) ...No. It's perfect. Don't let it go to your head.
Because you're honest with me. That's twice in my life I've found that.

steps.say: When I closed my diner, I thought that part of my life was finished. Then I walked in here and you told me the truth about your cooking, and you listened to an old lady ramble, and you made me soup every time I was sad without me ever saying so.
I want you to have the recipe. And the bell. It hung over my door for fifty years. It ought to hang over a door again.

choices.reply: Good. Make sure it rings. A quiet bell is a sad thing.

choices.text: Are you sure? This is Walter's.
choices.reply: It's yours now, dear. That's what he'd want. He'd have liked you very much.

choices.text: Thank you, Mabel. I'll take care of it.
choices.reply: I know you will. I've watched you take care of everyone.

steps.say: Now. We eat. Two bowls. And then I'm going home, because I'm ninety-one and it's past my bedtime.

steps.narrate: (You eat together at her window table while the rain slows down.)
(A horn honks outside. Twice. Then a little tune. Cheddar strolls in, twirling a set of keys on one finger.)

steps.say: Guess who got his car back from the shop? This guy. Guess who knows a secret beach? Also this guy.
So here's the deal. After closing: you, the whole crew, my car, the beach. Fishing off the pier, shells on the sand, and me, being delightful.

choices.reply: YES. I mean. Cool. Cool cool cool. That's cool.
It's so secret even the map doesn't know. Okay, it's on the map. But nobody reads maps!
Can I drive. CAN I DRIVE. ...Mostly forward. Very well, forward.

steps.say: I'll park out front after hours. Just come find me. Don't be strangers, [nickname]!

steps.narrate: (He jingles the keys one more time on his way out. The horn honks again from the street: the same little tune.)
(Mabel stays in her seat after everyone else has gone, buttoning and unbuttoning her coat.)

steps.say: I've been thinking, dear. Which at my age is a whole afternoon's work.
You lot ought to come round to mine. For tea. The house with the window boxes, just along from here. Tuesday.

choices.reply: Good. After closing. Don't be late. I can't abide late. Walter was late to our wedding. Twenty minutes. I've never let him forget it.
Tuesday. Or whichever day it is when you come. I lose track. Walter kept the calendar.
The one with flowers that aren't dead. You'd be surprised how few of those there are.

steps.say: Knock properly, mind. None of that tapping. And don't be late.

steps.narrate: (At the door she turns back.) Wednesday! ...No. Whenever. Don't be late! (And she's gone.)
(Stitches lingers by the door after closing, turning his hat around and around in his paws.)

steps.say: Um. [name]? Can I ask something? You can say no. You'll probably say no. That's okay.
I have a house. Well, everyone has a house. Not everyone. Sorry. I mean, I live in one. Near here. And maybe, if you wanted, you could... visit? It. Me. The house with me in it.

choices.reply: You would? Really? Oh. Okay. Okay! I'll tidy. I'll tidy so much.
The blue one. With the patches. I patched the house too. Is that weird? It had holes.
There's always hot chocolate. I mean. I'll buy some. There will be hot chocolate.

steps.say: So. After closing. Any night. If you want. No pressure. Some pressure. Nice pressure. ...I'm going to go now.

steps.narrate: (He walks into the door frame on his way out, apologizes to it, and leaves.)
(A drumroll from the dining room. It's Cheddar, drumming on a table with two spoons.)

steps.say: Ladies and gentlemen! Chefs of all ages! Gather round, gather round, for an announcement of TREMENDOUS importance!
The Cheddar residence, home of the one and only Cheddar, is hereby OPEN to visitors! Specifically you! After hours! Free admission!

choices.reply: Ha! I knew it. I already told the house. It's very excited. Houses can't be excited. Mine is.
The yellow one with the lights and the star. You can't miss it. People have tried. They can't.
The only trick is how charming the place is. And a small hole in the porch. Mind the hole.

steps.say: Knock any night after closing. Knock loud. Knock with flair. I'll know it's you, [nickname].

steps.narrate: (He takes a deep bow, knocks a spoon off the table, and bows to that too on his way out.)
